title: Decouple input warmup and decode with async slice coordinator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background and motivation: In live workloads we observe frequent stalls when the pipeline ties input warmup (prefill) and decode stages at the slice granularity. Large-batch and high-concurrency traces show that a slow decode on one worker can back pressure prefill across other slices leading to elevated p95/p99 tail latency. This PR introduces an asynchronous slice coordinator that decouples input warmup from decode execution so prefill can make forward progress (KV priming + prefix materialization) without waiting for the decode stage to accept the same slice.

Design summary: the async slice coordinator is a small scheduling layer between the prefill producer and decode consumers. Key ideas: (1) slices produced by prefill are transferred into an in-memory non-blocking transfer queue along with lightweight metadata (sequence id, prefix hash, kv-ready flag) so they can be consumed independently; (2) decoders subscribe to available slices and request per-slice admission tokens from the coordinator using a windowed backpressure allocator to preserve latency SLOs; (3) KV cache now exposes a soft-commit operation that marks a slice's KV entries as warm without forcing a full synchronous flush—this enables fast lookup by decode kernels while avoiding immediate global book-keeping; and (4) minimal kernel surface changes: a non-blocking slice descriptor and a tiny handshake API for kernel readiness checks.

Why this is different: instead of speculative duplication of prefill work or heavy-weight handoffs, this approach focuses on slice-level asynchrony and lightweight metadata exchange to keep memory overhead low and reduce decode-induced stalls across unrelated slices. It is complementary to speculative prefill and microbatch coalescing, but targets workloads where inter-slice decode variance is the dominant source of tail latency.

Implementation notes: C++ runtime changes live under src/runtime/scheduler/: async_slice_coordinator.{cpp,h} implements the transfer queue and token allocator; kernel streaming changes are limited to kernel_stream.cpp for the readiness API; src/runtime/kv/cache_sync.cpp adds soft_commit and lookup hints. Unit tests and microbenchmarks were added under tests/benchmark/latency/async_slice_bench.py and tests/unit/scheduler/test_async_slice_coordinator.py. The implementation uses lock-free single-producer single-consumer queues where possible and falls back to wait-free ring buffers for multi-consumer paths.

Testing and verification: local unit tests and CI passed (see checks). Perf harness showed consistent improvements: mixed prefill/decode synthetic traces (seq-len distribution skewed to long decodes) yield 12% throughput improvement under steady load and 18% reduction in p95 end-to-end latency in our internal benchmark cluster. Memory overhead measured at +6% resident set for large model configs (4k token warmup windows) and was within the safety budget.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in ENG-1893
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Perf benchmarks added and recorded
- [x] Metrics emitted for coordinator queue depth and per-slice wait time
- [x] No user-facing API changes

Rollback plan: feature is behind a runtime flag (runtime.async_slice_coordinator=false). If we observe regressions in the canary lane we can disable flag and revert commit cluster-wide.

Notes for reviewers: focus on memory reclamation on the ring buffer, metric naming for per-slice timers, and correctness of KV soft_commit semantics under race.
commit_summary: Initial coordinator scaffolding and non-blocking queue implementation
Implement token allocator and admission protocol for slices
Add KV soft_commit API and integrate with slice producer
Kernel readiness API and small kernel_stream changes
Unit tests and perf harness + docs
review_comments: Rohan Patel: Can you quantify peak memory usage for 4k warmup windows and explain reclamation semantics? Some of our canary traces had larger resident growth previously.

Maya Chen: Measured +6% resident set on our benchmark cluster; coordinator uses an epoch-based reclamation for slice descriptors and we added a config knob to cap queued slices per-model to prevent unbounded growth.
Rohan Patel: Please add a unit test that simulates delayed decoder so we can guard against pathological enqueueing.
Maya Chen: Added delayed decoder test (tests/unit/scheduler/test_async_slice_coordinator.py::test_delayed_consumer) which asserts queue cap behavior and correct soft_commit ordering.
Lena Ortiz: Metric names look fine but prefer suffix '.ms' for per_slice_wait histogram. Also suggest emitting a synthetic 'slice_migration' counter for debugging cross-worker handoffs.
Maya Chen: Renamed per_slice_wait to per_slice_wait_ms and added slice_migration counter. Updated docs/architecture.
Evan Brooks: Verified that kernel readiness API keeps kernel changes minimal and didn't regress streaming decode throughput in my local runs. Approving.
CI bot: buildkite/ci passed, unit tests passed, perf checks improved for target traces.
release_notes: runtime: add async slice coordinator to decouple input warmup from decode, reducing tail latency for workloads with high decode variance. Controlled by runtime.async_slice_coordinator flag; no public API changes.
perf_summary: Mixed prefill/decode synthetic: +12% throughput, -18% p95 latency; p99 unchanged in steady-state. Memory overhead: +6% RSS for large warmup windows (config cap available). Benchmarks run on internal perf cluster (8xA100), harness scripts added under tests/benchmark.
notes: This change is intended to be a low-risk performance improvement for production workloads. We left the default off on release branches until the canary lane completes a 2-week soak.
